I build the infrastructure around AI models (human in the loop, non cached data for agents) to build coherent AI products.

For the last two years I've done this on my own, shipping production agentic systems end to end and learning the hard tradeoffs by hitting them.

- Iridium (Linkedin MCP) built to help people scale their outreach thoughtfully. Connect to Claude to comment on relevant posts, discover relevant ppl in the industry and schedule your outreach. All Agentic Calls are tracked, nothing happens without final human approval. 

- vLLM EKS Multi-tenant vLLM + diffusion pools on AWS EKS, autoscaled on queue depth, not CPU, because queue dept

recent_posts.text:
I demo'd Iridium - LinkedIn Agent live yesterday!

It's a tool built to delegate tasks like outreach to your agents (Claude / ChatGPT). Agent actions take place only after explicit user approval, and they can use your other connectors (Notion, Salesforce, Glean) to complete repeated outreach actions.

It's useful for bringing capable candidates and hiring managers together quicker.

In the clip: I

I gave a 5 min demo of Iridium at Hackerdojo in MTV 

Got some great feedback from people (chatgpt is more b2c friendly)

Noticed that some people were confused on some aspects of the service (is it a skill or a connector, how does the human in the loop work).

The QnA session after the demo helped me find most of the gaps in Iridium's narrative.

I built an agent inside Claude that runs my LinkedIn engagement. It drafts every comment in my voice, grounded in fresh and accurate context, and turns hours of work into a few minutes of review. 

Nothing goes out without my approval.

Demo below. Comment "IRIDIUM" for early access.

#AI #Agents #MCP
